traceability.notes:
All functional, configuration, and documentation aspects described in docs/stories/010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-SUPPORTS.story.md are implemented and verified.
Key points: - The ESLint rule implementation exists (src/rules/prefer-implements-annotation.ts) and is fully traced to this story and its requirement IDs. - The plugin exposes `traceability/prefer-supports-annotation` as the primary rule name and `traceability/prefer-implements-annotation` as a deprecated alias, matching REQ-RULE-NAME and the Rule Naming acceptance criterion, even though the checkbox in the story file remains unchecked. - The rule is a suggestion-type, disabled by default (not present in recommended/strict configs), and can be configured via standard ESLint severities (off/warn/error), satisfying REQ-OPTIONAL-WARNING, REQ-CONFIG-SEVERITY, and the associated acceptance criteria for configurable enforcement and backward compatibility. - Auto-fix is implemented conservatively: simple single-story @story + @req blocks are converted into a single @supports line while preserving formatting and placement; complex or ambiguous blocks are reported but not auto-fixed, ensuring valid output. - Multi-story or mixed @story/@req/@supports patterns are detected and reported without auto-fix, matching REQ-MULTI-STORY-DETECT and the intended non-fixable warning behavior. - Legacy @story/@req annotations and existing @supports annotations continue to be validated by other rules, and remain valid regardless of this rule’s setting. - Documentation (internal rule doc, migration guide, API reference) thoroughly explains purpose, configuration, auto-fix behavior, limitations, and aliasing. - Dedicated tests cover all these behaviors and pass in the current Jest run.
Given this concrete evidence, all acceptance criteria and detailed requirements for story 010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-SUPPORTS are satisfied by the current implementation.
